findings.title: Extraction API has no authentication
findings.cwe: CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function
findings.owasp: OWASP API Security Top 10 API2; OWASP Top 10 A01 Broken Access Control
findings.component: FastAPI app in app.py, published by nginx location /extract/
findings.location: app.py:136-147 and route handlers at app.py:44377, 46231, 47531, 47666, 47708
findings.description: Every application route is registered without a FastAPI dependency, API-key check, or authentication middleware. The HTTP middleware only counts in-flight requests. nginx location /extract/ proxies to 127.0.0.1:8001 with no auth_request and no allow/deny rule. Interactive documentation is left at the FastAPI defaults.
findings.root_cause: Routes trust the network path. The application does not authenticate the caller.
findings.impact: Any client who can reach port 8001 or https://zydus-py.mediola.in/extract/ can call extraction, read operational health, and download the API schema. Laravel authorization, if any, is not enforced here. A customer invoice was not submitted during this assessment.
findings.recommendation: Require a shared credential or mutual TLS between the Laravel application and this service, and reject missing credentials with HTTP 401. Restrict the nginx location to the application servers. Disable /docs, /redoc, and /openapi.json on the public vhost.
findings.verification: After the control is added, repeat an unauthenticated GET /extract/docs and an empty POST /extract/split-and-extract. Both should be HTTP 401 or HTTP 403, and the public vhost should not serve the schema.
findings.preconditions: Network reachability of port 8001 or the nginx /extract/ location. No account is required.
findings.limitations: Cross-tenant document access was not attempted. Availability impact from repeated calls was not measured.
findings.sast_evidence: app.py constructs FastAPI() with no docs_url override and adds only CORSMiddleware plus an in-flight counter. Handlers split_and_extract_invoices, test_extract, extract_pod_grn_endpoint, and extract_sales_statement_endpoint declare no security dependency. Live OpenAPI securitySchemes is null.
findings.dast_evidence: From 127.0.0.1:8001 with no Authorization header: GET /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json, /health, and / returned HTTP 200. POST /split-and-extract and POST /extract-pod-grn with an empty body returned HTTP 400, not HTTP 401. POST /test-extract and POST /extract-sales-statement returned HTTP 422 field-required, not HTTP 401. The same documentation URL through nginx https://zydus-py.mediola.in/extract/docs returned HTTP 200. No WWW-Authenticate header was present.

findings.title: split_raw_url is fetched without a destination allow list
findings.owasp: OWASP API Security Top 10 API7; OWASP Top 10 A10 SSRF
findings.description: When a caller omits the upload file and supplies split_raw_url, both handlers pass that value to requests.get with a 120-second timeout and no scheme, host, port, or redirect allow list. The downloaded bytes are then treated as the document to parse. The routes are unauthenticated.
findings.root_cause: The form field is used as a request URL. requests follows redirects by default.
findings.impact: A reachable caller can cause the server to issue an HTTP GET to a destination it names, including addresses the server can reach. This assessment did not send a URL and did not request cloud-metadata or internal addresses. Impact beyond the code path was therefore not demonstrated.
findings.recommendation: Remove arbitrary URL fetch, or accept only HTTPS URLs on an explicit storage-host list. Do not follow redirects onto a different host. Require authentication before any fetch. Return a generic error instead of the client exception text.
findings.verification: On a non-production instance, submit a URL outside the allow list and confirm the service does not open a connection and does not echo resolver or connection errors. Confirm an allow-listed storage URL still works for the Laravel caller.
findings.preconditions: Reachability of the unauthenticated route. No live fetch was performed in this assessment.
findings.confidence: High for the code path. Runtime behavior was not re-executed.
findings.limitations: A server-side fetch was not sent. Cloud-metadata and internal-network destinations were not requested. A September 2026 assessment recorded a loopback fetch; that test was not repeated and is not used as this assessment's proof.
findings.sast_evidence: split_and_extract_invoices calls requests.get(split_raw_url, timeout=120) and writes response.content to the temp file. extract_pod_grn_endpoint uses the same call and then parses the body. No urlparse host check precedes either call.
findings.dast_evidence: Not performed. Sending a URL would make the production worker connect outbound. The empty POST only confirmed that the parameter is still accepted as an alternative to a file upload (HTTP 400 names split_raw_url).

findings.title: Caller-supplied blob container and path are used with the service credential
findings.owasp: OWASP API Security Top 10 API1 Broken Object Level Authorization
findings.description: blob_container overrides the configured container. split_raw_blob_path is passed to download_blob().readall() with the process Azure credential. target_invoices_blob_folder becomes the upload prefix, and upload_blob is called with overwrite=True. A successful upload returns a read SAS built from the account key, valid for 24 hours. The same fields are accepted by /extract-pod-grn and by the live /extract-sales-statement handler.
findings.root_cause: Storage identity is the service account. Object names and the container name come from the request, and the routes are unauthenticated.
findings.impact: If the reviewed code is the code that is loaded, a caller who can reach the route can name a blob to read and a prefix to write, then receive a read URL. This assessment did not read or write an Azure object. No customer blob access is claimed.
findings.recommendation: Ignore client container names. Authorize blob operations against a fixed container and a server-generated prefix. Do not return an account-key SAS to an anonymous caller. After authentication exists, prefer a short-lived user-delegation SAS.
findings.verification: On a non-production storage account, send a foreign container and blob name and confirm the API rejects them. Confirm a legitimate Laravel upload still lands in the server-chosen prefix and that the response does not contain an account-key SAS.
findings.preconditions: Azure credentials are loaded in the process environment. A live storage call was intentionally not made.
findings.confidence: High for the code path. Storage access was not demonstrated.
findings.limitations: No blob read, overwrite, or SAS URL was requested. Credential values were not recorded.
findings.sast_evidence: container_name falls back to AZURE_CONTAINER_NAME only when blob_container is empty. get_blob_client(container=container_name, blob=split_raw_blob_path) is followed by download_blob().readall(). upload_split_pdf_to_blob builds blob_name from target_invoices_blob_folder and returns blob_client.url plus a read SAS.
findings.dast_evidence: Not performed. A production blob read or write was out of scope.

findings.title: Environment file holding cloud and model credentials is world-readable
findings.cwe: CWE-732 Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
findings.description: The environment file mode is 644, owner root, group root. Non-empty values are present for the model API keys, the Azure storage connection string, and the Azure account key. The Google credential file named by the environment is mode 600. HTTP retrieval of /.env does not return the file.
findings.root_cause: The secrets file is world-readable. The service runs as root and does not need world read.
findings.impact: Any local account can read the cloud storage and model credentials in this file. This is not a public HTTP download.
findings.recommendation: Change the file to mode 600, or 640 with a dedicated service group. Move secrets to a secret store. Rotate the credentials that have been stored in the world-readable file.
findings.verification: stat the file and confirm mode 600 or 640. Repeat GET /.env and confirm the body is still the banner or HTTP 404, never the file.
findings.preconditions: Local filesystem access. No secret values were copied into the report.
findings.sast_status: Confirmed by file mode and configuration review
findings.dast_status: Confirmed that HTTP does not return the file
findings.limitations: Values and the Google credential path were not written to the report. Whether a non-root local account exists was not enumerated.
findings.sast_evidence: stat mode 644 root:root. Key names were checked by length only. The Google application-credential file mode is 600.
findings.dast_evidence: GET https://zydus-py.mediola.in/.env via a loopback resolve returned HTTP 200, Content-Length 35, body equal to the nginx banner. It did not return the environment file.

findings.title: API listens in cleartext on all interfaces
findings.cwe: CWE-319 Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
findings.location: runner.py:22-28; live unit ExecStart runs runner.py; iptables INPUT policy ACCEPT
findings.description: runner.py sets host 0.0.0.0 and port 8001. The live socket is 0.0.0.0:8001. ufw is inactive and the iptables INPUT policy is ACCEPT. nginx already publishes the same application over TLS at /extract/. A GET of /health on the host's own primary address, port 8001, returned HTTP 200 with server uvicorn. An off-box Internet scan was not performed.
findings.root_cause: The process binds every IPv4 interface and the host firewall does not restrict the port.
findings.impact: Document uploads and any future API key sent to port 8001 would travel without TLS. The nginx body-size limit and TLS terminator do not apply to this port. The assessment sent only a health GET.
findings.recommendation: Bind 127.0.0.1 and publish the service only through the nginx TLS vhost. If a direct port is required, firewall it to the Laravel servers.
findings.verification: Confirm ss shows 127.0.0.1:8001 only, and a request to the host primary address on port 8001 fails.
findings.preconditions: The socket is bound. Off-box filtering in front of the host was not tested.
findings.sast_status: Confirmed in runner.py and the live unit
findings.confidence: High for the local bind. External Internet exposure was not scanned from a second host.
findings.limitations: nmap was not installed. No document was sent over cleartext. Bandit B104 matches this bind.
findings.sast_evidence: runner.py HOST = 0.0.0.0, PORT = 8001, proxy_headers = True. The __main__ block in app.py also defaults --host to 0.0.0.0; the live process uses runner.py.
findings.dast_evidence: ss shows 0.0.0.0:8001. curl to http://148.230.66.182:8001/health from this host returned HTTP 200, server uvicorn.

findings.title: Unauthenticated health output includes the in-flight document identity
findings.owasp: OWASP Top 10 A01 Broken Access Control
findings.description: GET /health returns processing state, model name, memory, uptime, and the current request's source file name, batch id, and request id. During this assessment an extraction was in progress. Those three fields were populated. The values were removed from stored evidence and are not reproduced here. GET /ready returns a smaller snapshot that includes request id and stage.
findings.root_cause: Operational telemetry intended for the caller is exposed on an unauthenticated route.
findings.impact: A remote caller can learn that a document is being processed and can learn its file name and batch identifier while the job is active.
findings.recommendation: Remove document identifiers from unauthenticated probes. Keep a detailed health document on an authenticated management path.
findings.verification: Call GET /health and GET /ready with no credentials while a job is active. The body should not contain a file name, batch id, or request id.
findings.preconditions: A job must be in progress for the identifier fields to be non-empty. The route itself is always anonymous.
findings.limitations: The captured file name and batch id were redacted. current_invoice was null in the captured body.
findings.sast_evidence: The health snapshot copies source_filename, batch_id, request_id, current_invoice, page, and stage from the in-process progress structure.
findings.dast_evidence: GET /health on 127.0.0.1:8001, through nginx, and on the cleartext public address returned HTTP 200. The redacted body marks source_filename, batch_id, and request_id as present. current_model was gemini-2.5-flash-lite. Memory and uptime were included.

findings.title: Handlers return exception text to the caller
findings.cwe: CWE-209 Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
findings.component: HTTPException(detail=str(e)) on extraction handlers and blob upload
findings.description: Broad exception handlers pass str(e) into HTTPException. Validation failures observed in this assessment returned FastAPI's normal field errors or a fixed string, not a traceback. The exception-text path was not triggered, because doing so required a failing URL fetch or a storage error.
findings.root_cause: Exception text is treated as a client-facing detail.
findings.impact: A later failure can return internal host names, storage errors, or upstream text to an unauthenticated caller. That response was not captured in this assessment.
findings.recommendation: Return a stable error code to clients. Write the exception only to the server log.
findings.verification: Force a handled failure on a non-production instance and confirm the JSON body has no library exception text.
findings.preconditions: The code path exists. This assessment did not provoke HTTP 500.
findings.confidence: High for the source pattern. The sensitive HTTP 500 body was not reproduced.
findings.limitations: Empty posts returned HTTP 400 or HTTP 422 without stack traces. That does not exercise detail=str(e).
findings.sast_evidence: upload_split_pdf_to_blob, test_extract, both sales-statement handlers, and extract_pod_grn_endpoint raise HTTPException with detail=str(e) or detail=str(last_err).
findings.dast_evidence: Empty POSTs returned fixed validation JSON. No traceback and no credential text were present in those bodies.

findings.title: CORS reflects any origin and allows credentials
findings.description: allow_origins is ["*"], allow_credentials is True, and methods and headers are ["*"]. A preflight from Origin https://untrusted.example received that origin reflected and access-control-allow-credentials: true. The service does not set a session cookie, so browser credential theft was not demonstrated.
findings.root_cause: Wildcard origin combined with credentialed CORS. Starlette reflects the request origin when credentials are enabled.
findings.impact: If cookie authentication is added later, any website could make credentialed browser calls. Today the demonstrated issue is the policy itself.
findings.recommendation: Allow only the Laravel origins. Do not combine a reflected origin with allow_credentials unless that origin is trusted.
findings.verification: Repeat the preflight from an unapproved origin and confirm the allow-origin header is absent.
findings.preconditions: A browser client. The current integration observed in prior operations is server-to-server.
findings.limitations: No session cookie was issued, so data was not read cross-origin.
findings.dast_evidence: OPTIONS /health with Origin https://untrusted.example returned HTTP 200, access-control-allow-origin: https://untrusted.example, access-control-allow-credentials: true, and allow-methods including DELETE, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH, POST, PUT.

findings.title: Security headers are absent and server versions are disclosed
findings.cwe: CWE-693 Protection Mechanism Failure; CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information
findings.description: The HTTPS health response identified Server: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) and did not send Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, or Referrer-Policy. Direct responses on port 8001 identified server: uvicorn. Port 80 redirects to HTTPS. The TLS certificate for zydus-py.mediola.in is valid through 16 December 2026, and a TLS 1.2 handshake succeeded.
findings.root_cause: Default nginx and uvicorn headers. The extraction location adds no security headers and does not hide the server token.
findings.impact: Version tokens aid reconnaissance. The missing browser headers matter if a browser client uses the documentation pages. No session compromise was shown.
findings.recommendation: Hide version tokens. Add HSTS on the HTTPS vhost and a baseline of X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and a restrictive Content-Security-Policy for any HTML documentation that remains.
findings.verification: Repeat GET /extract/health and confirm the Server header has no version and HSTS is present.
findings.limitations: TLS configuration was sampled with one TLS 1.2 handshake. A full cipher sweep was not run.
findings.sast_evidence: The /extract/ location sets proxy headers and timeouts only. client_max_body_size is 500M at server scope. No add_header directives are on this location.
findings.dast_evidence: nginx health response had Server: nginx/1.24.0 (Ubuntu) and none of the headers named above. Port 8001 responses had server: uvicorn. HTTP /extract/health returned 301 to HTTPS.

findings.title: Upload size and concurrency limits do not cover every extraction route
findings.vector: Availability impact was not tested, so no CVSS score is assigned.
findings.cwe: CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
findings.owasp: OWASP API Security Top 10 API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption
findings.location: app.py:139, app.py:234, app.py:44470, app.py:46231; nginx client_max_body_size 500M
findings.description: Request.max_body_size = 200MB is assigned on the Starlette Request class. That attribute is not implemented by the installed Starlette 0.45.3, so the assignment does not enforce a limit. After the bytes are read, the handlers log the size and do not reject it. /split-and-extract acquires a semaphore of MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS, which is 1 in the live environment, with a queue timeout of 3600 seconds. /test-extract, /extract-sales-statement, and /extract-pod-grn do not acquire that semaphore. nginx allows a 500 MB body. No per-client rate limit was found. A load test was not performed.
findings.root_cause: The body cap is not enforced in the application, and the single-flight gate is applied only to the primary route.
findings.impact: A small number of large or concurrent extraction calls can occupy the one worker. That outcome was not measured and is not claimed as an outage.
findings.recommendation: Enforce one authenticated size cap before OCR, on every extraction route, and align nginx with it. Put every extraction route on the same queue. Remove or firewall /test-extract.
findings.verification: Submit a body above the chosen cap and confirm HTTP 413 before OCR starts. Confirm /test-extract is absent or authenticated.
findings.preconditions: The control gap is visible in source. Resource exhaustion was intentionally not tested.
findings.sast_status: Confirmed in source and nginx configuration
findings.confidence: High for the missing control. Low for availability impact, which was not measured.
findings.limitations: No oversized body and no concurrent upload were sent. Rate limiting is therefore unverified as an effective control; the absence of an application limiter is confirmed by review.
findings.sast_evidence: Starlette Request has no max_body_size. Only split_and_extract_invoices calls request_processing_semaphore.acquire. The live environment reports MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=1.
findings.dast_evidence: OpenAPI lists POST /test-extract. No load or oversized request was sent.

findings.title: The extraction process runs as root
findings.description: The unit sets User=root and Group=root. The live process uid is 0. No command injection, deserialization, or template-execution issue was confirmed that would turn this into code execution.
findings.root_cause: The unit was written to run as root.
findings.impact: A future parser flaw in PDF, image, or OCR code would run as root. That flaw was not shown.
findings.recommendation: Run the service as a dedicated unprivileged user with write access only to its temporary and log directories.
findings.verification: Restart under the service account and confirm the listener uid is not 0.
findings.limitations: No privilege-escalation test was required or performed.
findings.sast_evidence: /etc/systemd/system/split-extract.service sets User=root and Group=root. The repository copy under deploy/systemd/ is not the file systemd is using; the live unit starts runner.py.

findings.title: Container build file does not match the running service
findings.vector: The container is not the running deployment.
findings.location: Dockerfile COPY app5.py and CMD python app5.py
findings.description: The Dockerfile copies app5.py, which is not in the tree, installs packages as root, and listens on 0.0.0.0:8001. docker-compose publishes port 8001 and reads a local .env. The live process is the virtualenv interpreter executing runner.py under systemd. No container was running this service.
findings.root_cause: The image definition was not updated when the entry point became runner.py.
findings.impact: An operator who deploys the compose file would not reproduce the service that was tested. This is not a live exposure.
findings.recommendation: Point the image at the current application, run as a non-root user, and do not publish port 8001 if nginx is the only front door.
findings.verification: A test build should fail or be updated until the image entry point matches runner.py or app:app.
findings.preconditions: File review. Docker was not used to start this service.
findings.sast_evidence: Dockerfile line 25 copies app5.py. No app5.py exists in the project. The live command line is runner.py.
findings.dast_evidence: Not applicable. The listener is a host process, not a container.

findings.title: Dependency advisories are present; exploitability was not demonstrated
findings.vector: Scanner output is not an application CVSS score.
findings.cwe: CWE-1104 Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
findings.owasp: OWASP Top 10 A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components
findings.component: Virtual environment /var/www/html/venv used by the running service
findings.location: Installed distributions under site-packages. Direct requirements are unpinned minimums in requirements.txt.
findings.description: pip-audit 2.10.1, pointed at the production site-packages and not at a reinstall, reported 109 advisory records. De-duplicated identifiers total 70, across 12 packages. No advisory was exploited. Packages on the document path include pillow 11.1.0, python-multipart 0.0.20, starlette 0.45.3, pdfminer-six 20231228, PyPDF2 3.0.1, requests 2.32.3, and urllib3 2.7.0. The fix versions reported by the tool are in scans/pip_audit_summary.json. An earlier invocation that tried to re-resolve the freeze file failed on cffi==2.0.0 and was discarded.
findings.root_cause: Installed packages are below fix versions reported by the advisory database on the day of the scan.
findings.impact: Unknown until each advisory is compared with the code paths this service uses. This item is patch input, not a demonstrated breach.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade in a test environment, starting with pillow, python-multipart, starlette, and the PDF libraries. Re-run pip-audit and retest invoice extraction. Do not upgrade the production environment as part of this assessment.
findings.verification: pip-audit against the same site-packages reports no advisories, or each remaining identifier is accepted with a written reason.
findings.preconditions: Advisory data was retrieved from the tool's default service on 22 October 2026.
findings.sast_status: Scanner result, not a validated vulnerability
findings.confidence: High that the scanner reported these identifiers. No confidence in exploitability.
findings.limitations: Individual advisory CVSS scores were not revalidated. No exploit was run. Transitive packages were included because they are installed.
findings.sast_evidence: scans/pip_audit.json and scans/pip_audit_summary.json. Counts: 109 records, 70 unique identifiers, 12 packages.
